subsystems.name: Sensing layer
subsystems.role: measures what the city is doing, continuously.

subsystems.name: Communications and edge compute
subsystems.role: moves data and runs control logic close to where it is needed.
parts: edge servers in substations and signal cabinets

subsystems.name: City state model
subsystems.role: a single shared, continuously updated estimate of what is happening, backed by a simulated twin of the city.

subsystems.name: Actuation layer
subsystems.role: interfaces to the physical equipment that can actually be commanded.

subsystems.name: Agent orchestration
subsystems.role: software that proposes or takes actions in bounded domains, with negotiation between domains.

subsystems.name: Security and governance
subsystems.role: keeps a city-scale control system from being hijacked or misused.

buildSteps.title: Instrument a district
buildSteps.detail: Smart meters, counters, environmental sensors and cabinets are installed across a few square kilometres, with clear rules on what is collected and what is not.

buildSteps.title: Build the data platform
buildSteps.detail: Municipal departments, utilities and transit agencies agree on shared schemas and publish real-time feeds through APIs instead of keeping them in silos.

buildSteps.title: Build a calibrated twin
buildSteps.detail: A simulated version of the district — road network, electrical feeders, water mains — is tuned until its outputs match measured behaviour from the past year.

buildSteps.title: Close one control loop
buildSteps.detail: A single function, such as traffic-signal timing or building demand response, is optimised automatically within narrow limits, with an operator able to overrule it. Safety limits are baked into the software, not left to the model.

buildSteps.title: Add forecasting and simulation
buildSteps.detail: The twin is run ahead of real time to predict congestion, peak load or flooding, and to test a policy change on the model before applying it on the street.

buildSteps.title: Introduce scoped agents
buildSteps.detail: Each domain gets a software agent with a tight objective and hard constraints — for example, re-timing signals to cut queue length while keeping pedestrian green time above a minimum. These are narrow controllers, not general intelligences.

buildSteps.title: Federate the domains
buildSteps.detail: Energy, transport and water agents share one state estimate and negotiate trade-offs, such as charging a bus fleet when grid capacity is spare, with a rule set for resolving conflicts.

buildSteps.title: Scale out and harden
buildSteps.detail: Redundancy, offline fallback modes and cyber-security reviews are extended as coverage grows; every automated decision is logged and reversible.

buildSteps.title: Attempt general autonomy
buildSteps.detail: A city-scale system that sets its own goals and rewrites its own objectives across all domains would require general artificial intelligence, which does not exist and is not on any verified timetable.

prerequisites.why: cities already deploy metering, counting and environmental sensors at district scale.
several cities run twins for planning and flood or traffic modelling, but few close a real-time control loop.
control decisions in the tens of milliseconds need fibre or private cellular, not consumer links.
reinforcement learning and model predictive control have been demonstrated on cooling, dispatch and signal timing, but never over a whole city.
the 'sentient' part assumes an AGI that can set its own goals; this does not exist and cannot be engineered from today's tooling.

prerequisites.tech: Cybersecurity and privacy at civic scale
prerequisites.why: a single system that can steer traffic and power is also a single point of failure and a high-value target.

pathway.milestone: districts with instrumented assets and dashboards
pathway.unlocks: visibility — operators see problems sooner, but the city still acts manually.

pathway.milestone: closed-loop control of one or two domains with human oversight
pathway.unlocks: measurable savings in energy peak load and intersection delays.

pathway.milestone: a shared twin and state estimate across departments
pathway.unlocks: cross-domain trade-offs, such as aligning electric fleet charging with grid headroom.

pathway.milestone: federated multi-domain agents under a regulator-approved rulebook
pathway.unlocks: city-wide optimisation with provable safety limits.

pathway.milestone: self-directed city governance by a general AI
pathway.unlocks: nothing that can currently be engineered; this remains a design fiction, not a roadmap.
